title: How Wood and Allen met; which band Barbarin played with
summary: Wood says they met through the Tulane history department and Hogan; they guess Barbarin was with Eureka or Young Tuxedo, with substitutes common.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, well, I mean, to me this is interesting because I've never talked to many people about this. How did we get to know each other?

You and I? Yeah. Through just being in this history department at Tulane. I guess in Hogan probably had said something to me sometime about you. And I probably hunted you up and said, listen, you know, I hear you're interested in the music. And I am too. Where do I go to get to hear something? And you were forthcoming and said, well, you know, come to a parade. There's going to be some things. And then I remember very well, you were very regular. You would call up maybe Friday afternoon or something and say, you know, there's going to be a parade, such and such a place. So if there was a funeral, you would tell me. Or I would see you on the campus and you'd tell me. Were you a graduate student in the history department then?
I was a graduate student around 56, yeah.
That would have been it. That would have been how we met.
But to get to know who was interested in jazz then, you know, it wasn't easy.
Yeah. I think that connection has probably came out of Hogan somehow. Yeah, that Hogan.
And I had said something to him about, you know, I'd like to, I was interested, I'd like to hear some music or something.
You don't remember what band Paul Barber was with. I'm curious.

It didn't register with you. It didn't really. My guess is it was either the Eureka or the, it was probably the Eureka. Because I don't think he played with the Young Tuxedo. It was either the Eureka or the Young Tuxedo. He might have played with the Young Tuxedo. I think he substituted them. Anywhere. Yeah.
In those bands. And membership was an important thing. But there were also substitutes.
You don't remember how those things happened 20, 30 years ago.
